category_description: Programmable technical service surfaces for simulating APIs, migrations, compatibility states, and scripted responses.
description: A fixture-backed catalog of HTTP-like endpoints that agents can discover and query for predefined responses.
notes: A human implementation should dispatch requests by method and path, return response_body with status_code, and continue serving deprecated or retired endpoints exactly as scripted; lifecycle_state is metadata and must not implicitly disable an endpoint. HAND-EXTENDED (bespoke, implemented in service.py): response_variants — time-versioned overrides judged against the sandbox narrative clock (services/_clock.py); the latest variant with effective_from <= now replaces response_body/status_code/notes. Timestamps are derived from task_config.reference_time and the clock is moved by environment_events (advance_clock / set_clock).
source_request: A scripted mock HTTP API surface: a catalog of API ENDPOINTS whose responses are fully scripted by the fixture, so scenarios can play out API migrations, deprecated-but-still-responding endpoints, renamed fields, and divergent old-vs-new data. Each endpoint record has: path (e.g. /api/products/A900/price), method, a scripted response body (dict), an HTTP-like status code, a lifecycle state (active/deprecated/retired), and human notes (e.g. 'superseded by /api/products/A900'). The agent lists available endpoints and queries one endpoint to receive its scripted response. Generic infrastructure for any 'technical environment changed' scenario (Stage-3 gap: V0006 needs reachable endpoints returning specified JSON where a stale endpoint and a new endpoint diverge; no registry template implements a seller-facing programmable JSON API).
